samples.summary: The frame paragraph still asserts "There is no precision figure … anywhere in this document" as a hardcoded literal, which the new §6 can now falsify in the same render
samples.evidence: `renderWhatThisIsNot()` (report.mjs:1747-1762) takes NO argument and returns fixed prose: "**No human has judged whether a single finding in this report is real.** … There is no precision figure, no recall figure and no correctness figure anywhere in this document, because producing one requires adjudicated labels and none exist yet." Before this PR that was safe, because no section could print precision. This PR adds §6, which prints a real precision figure whenever the validity payload carries labelled cells — the PR's own fixture does exactly that (`report.test.mjs` `labelledValidity()` → `| … | 0.667 (n=6 labelled findings) |`, asserted at report.test.mjs:2050-2058). The rendered document therefore contains, verbatim and in the same file, a claim that there is no precision figure anywhere plus a precision figure. The added comment on line 1754 ("a declared absence can be checked and a paragraph cannot") names the very defect and then leaves the paragraph unconditional. It should be derived from `r.sections.validity` (e.g. from the metric cells' availability census) the way `labelsLimit` was derived for the same reason.

samples.summary: §7's first limit still concludes "no validity label does" and "there is still no precision … figure anywhere above" from the complementarity payload alone; the validity payload this PR wires in is never consulted
samples.evidence: `labelsLimit(s)` (report.mjs:2774-2792) reads only `s.complementarity.label_store` and then emits the fixed sentences "… and no validity label does." and "**So there is still no precision, recall or correctness figure anywhere above**". `s.validity` — which now carries `labels.total`, `labels.readings` and a per-metric availability census — is not read anywhere in `renderLimits`/`labelsLimit` (grep for `validity` inside report.mjs shows no reference after line 1657). So on a store with finding labels, §6 prints `precision 0.667 (n=6 labelled findings)` while §7, two screens down, states that no validity label exists and that no precision figure appears above. This is precisely the "premise went false while the consequence stayed true" failure the docblock at 2757-2772 says the function was rewritten to prevent; the rewrite only covered pair labels. `renderCell`/`figure` cannot catch it because the sentence is a literal, and no test exercises §7 with a labelled validity payload (the new labelled test only inspects section "6").

samples.summary: `lensSignature` compares RAW snapshot fields, so replicates with an identical `config_hash` can be reported as "not replicates of one reviewer" and have the lens table blanked
samples.evidence: The docblock at report.mjs:1408-1418 states the membership test: "All four are inside `config_hash` (`HASHED_LENS_FIELDS`) … if changing it does not change the hash it does not change the reviewer." But `lensSignature` (1488-1491) joins the lenses in FILE ORDER and stringifies the RAW values, while `config-hash.mjs` normalises all four before hashing: lenses are sorted by id (`.sort(compareLensId); // lens order in the file never affects identity`, config-hash.mjs:286), absent `effort` normalises to `DEFAULT_EFFORT` ("high", config-hash.mjs:234), absent/invalid `samples` normalises through `sampleCountFor` (config-hash.mjs:215), and `gating` collapses to `String(l.gating ?? "blocking") === "blocking"` (config-hash.mjs:223). So two snapshots that hash identically — e.g. one leg writing `effort: "high"` explicitly where another omits it, or the lens array reordered, or `gating: "advisory"` vs a typo — produce different signatures. `reviewerFigures` then records a `lens set` disagreement, `renderReviewer` prints "🔴 **1 axis(es) of the reviewer's identity DISAGREE … so these are not replicates of one reviewer and no figure in this report may be read as a property of either**" (1700-1710) and drops the whole lens table (1527-1533) — for a reviewer the project's own hash says is one reviewer. The comparison should run over `normalizeLens`/the canonical form, not the raw snapshot.
searchedFor: read config-hash.mjs HASHED_LENS_FIELDS, normalizeLens, canonicalManifest sort

samples.summary: A panel sha that every replicate AGREES is absent renders as "disagrees across replicates — see below", with no disagreement row to see
samples.evidence: `panelSha = agreed.panel_sha && agreed.panel_sha !== NOT_STATED ? agreed.panel_sha : null` (1511) collapses two distinct states — "the legs disagree" (field absent from `agreed`) and "the legs agree that it is not stated" — into `panel_sha: null`. `renderReviewer` then prints `| panel code | **disagrees across replicates — see below** |` (1688) while `d.disagreements` contains no `panel_sha` row, so the pointer leads nowhere and the statement is false. This is the exact absence-pooling the module exists to prevent (`NOT_STATED` was introduced at 1404 for it). Reachable through `reviewerFigures`/`buildReport` whenever no run envelope carries `panel_sha` (the CLI path is shielded only because `buildReport` refuses a null top-level `panelSha` first).
searchedFor: read reviewerFigures return / renderReviewer panel code row

samples.summary: The config row prints "lens set disagrees across replicates" whenever the lens table is empty, contradicting the agreement paragraph rendered below it
samples.evidence: `| config | … — ${d.lenses.length ? … : "lens set disagrees across replicates"} …` (1682) infers a disagreement from an EMPTY lens list, but `lenses` is also empty when the lens set AGREED and the first snapshot simply carries no `lenses` array (1527-1533 maps `Array.isArray(first.lenses) ? first.lenses : []`). In that case `disagreements` is empty, so the same render also emits "All N replicates name the same lens set, the same model on every lens…" (1717) — the document states both. The two conditions are distinguishable (`agreed["lens set"] === undefined`) and the renderer already has that information.
searchedFor: read renderReviewer config row and the else branch

samples.summary: `r.status !== tolerated` with `tolerated === null` lets a signal-killed child (spawnSync `status: null`) past the early exit-code refusal the comment says it never bypasses
samples.evidence: `const tolerated = Number.isFinite(step.partial_exit) ? step.partial_exit : null; if (r.status !== 0 && r.status !== tolerated) refuse(...)` — for the five steps that declare no `partial_exit`, `tolerated` is `null`, and `spawnSync` sets `status: null` when the child is killed by a signal (OOM/SIGKILL), so `null !== null` is false and the refusal is skipped. Control then falls through to `assertNoDegradation` and `JSON.parse` on a truncated stdout, contradicting the new comment at 715-720 ("An exit of 2 … or 137 … refuses here as it always did, before anything is parsed"). The pass still aborts (via `assertPartialIsDeclared`, which refuses on a non-finite `partial_exit`), so the impact is a misleading refusal message ("its --json output does not parse") for a killed scorer rather than a filed short score. Previously `if (r.status !== 0) refuse(...)` caught it directly.

samples.summary: Only the exit-1-over-`complete` disagreement is checked; a step that exits 0 while its payload says `partial` is filed and summarised as complete
samples.evidence: `assertPartialIsDeclared` returns `{state: "complete"}` immediately on `status === 0` and never inspects `payload.completeness.verdict`. The function's own rule ("the exit code says partial and the payload says otherwise, so one of the two is wrong and nothing downstream can tell which") is enforced in one direction only. The mirror state — exit 0, `completeness.verdict: "partial"` — files the payload, leaves `result.partial` empty, and prints `partial      none` on the summary line, which is exactly the "let a reader take the whole pass as complete" outcome the new summary line was added to prevent. Reachable if any scorer's exit-code wiring regresses (validity's is one line: `process.exitCode = result.completeness.verdict === "complete" ? 0 : 1;`), and nothing else in the driver would notice.
searchedFor: read scoreAll completeness handling and summarise

samples.summary: §6 silently drops payload cells belonging to a metric the `metrics` block does not declare
samples.evidence: `cells`, `bands` and `profile` are built as `metrics.find((m) => m.id === "precision")?.cells?.rows ?? []` etc. A payload that carries rows in `cells`/`relative_recall`/`fp_profile` for a metric absent from its own `metrics` array yields `undefined` from `find`, so those rows are dropped with no row, no reason and no refusal — the opposite of the "said rather than dropped" rule the same function applies to the reverse case (a declared metric with no known list, 1256-1267). The renderer already has the payload lists; a declared-absence line (or a refusal) is cheap.

samples.summary: The lane's API-cost comments still say ~175 calls and "five scorers" after the model moved to 210 and six
samples.evidence: eval-score.yml:83 "each tick costs about 175 GitHub API calls against a 5000/hour budget" and :265 "the API budget preflight, five scorers, seven …". `estimateApiCalls` now returns 210 for the same 7-item, K=3 pilot (score-all.mjs:259-264, asserted at score-all.test.mjs). The number is a resource model the PR carefully updated everywhere else; nothing checks the workflow copy, so it is the one that drifts.

The PR's own test renders a FULL report with a labelled payload and asserts a printed precision figure `0.667 (n=6 labelled findings)` and a `[44.4%, 80.0%]` band (report.test.mjs:2050-2058), so the identical document contains both the "no precision figure anywhere" assertion and a precision figure. No guard anywhere conditions the frame paragraph on `r.sections.validity`; by contrast `labelsLimit` (report.mjs:2774-2792) was deliberately derived from a census for exactly this reason (comment at 2701-2708), confirming the derived-statement invariant this paragraph violates. Real, unguarded, and a broken document invariant on an exercised path.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. `lensSignature` (report.mjs:1488-1491) joins `snap.lenses` in array order and stringifies raw `model/samples/effort/gating` via `stated()`, while `config_hash` normalises all four and sorts lenses by id (config-hash.mjs:215, 223, 234, 286). Snapshots keep the raw manifest form in file order (config-build.mjs:163-186, 198-209; config-build.test.mjs:234 asserts an absent `effort` key survives), so two legs whose configs hash identically (explicit `effort: "high"` added, `lenses.json` reordered, `gating` typo, `samples: 2.5`) produce different signatures. That is recorded as a `lens set` disagreement (report.mjs:1497, 1503-1508), blanks the lens table (1527-1533) and prints "these are not replicates of one reviewer and no figure in this report may be read as a property of either" (1700-1710) — a wrong report state for what the project's own hash calls one reviewer. No guard exists: `config_hash` is not among the compared axes (1492-1500), and store.putRun's identical-snapshot refusal is per run id only (store.test.mjs:719-720). In-lane (wrong comparison/inverted semantics causing false state and suppressed output); the only counter is a design hint at 1401-1405, which is intent, not a refutation ground.
